description_full: Paysign, Inc. provides prepaid card programs, patient affordability offerings, digital banking, life science software technology solutions, and integrated payment processing services for businesses, consumers, and government institutions in the United States. The company offers solutions for corporate rewards, prepaid gift cards, general-purpose reloadable debit cards, employee incentives, consumer rebates, donor compensation, clinical trials, healthcare reimbursement payments and pharmaceutical payment assistance, and demand deposit accounts accessible with a debit card and software solutions. It also operates a customer service center; and offers a communication suite, including mobile app, two-way SMS, text alerts, and cardholder web portal. It markets its prepaid card solutions under the Paysign brand name. The company serves companies and municipalities that require payment solutions for rewards, rebates, payment assistance, and other payments to their customers, employees, agents, and others. Paysign, Inc. was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Henderson, Nevada.

financial_summary: Paysign, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $541M market cap on $82M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +29% over the past three years and +26% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 50% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $51M in free cash flow — roughly 62 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.95× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA.

Shareholder yield is only 0.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 21% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
